arxiv-2107-02360.title: Orthogonal root numbers of tempered parameters
arxiv-2107-02360.creator: David Schwein
arxiv-2107-02360.description: Abstract . We show that an orthogonal root number of a tempered L L -parameter φ \varphi decomposes as the product of two other numbers: the orthogonal root number of the principal parameter and the value on a certain involution of Langlands’s central character for φ \varphi .

arxiv-2107-08054.title: The reach of next-to-leading-order perturbation theory for the matter bispectrum 2021 The reach of next-to-leading-order perturbation theory for the matter bispectrum –
arxiv-2107-08054.creator: Davit Alkhanishvili, Cristiano Porciani, Emiliano Sefusatti, Matteo Biagetti, Andrei Lazanu, Andrea Oddo, Victoria Yankelevich
arxiv-2107-08054.description: Abstract We provide a comparison between the matter bispectrum derived with different flavours of perturbation theory at next-to-leading order and measurements from an unprecedentedly large suite of N N -body simulations. We use the χ 2 \chi^{2} goodness-of-fit test to determine the range of accuracy of the models as a function of the volume covered by subsets of the simulations.

arxiv-2204-10712.title: About block-parallel Boolean networks: a position paper
arxiv-2204-10712.creator: Jacques Demongeot, Sylvain Sené, [2mm] Université Grenoble Alpes, AGEIS EA 7407, 38000, Grenoble, France
arxiv-2204-10712.description: Abstract In automata networks, it is well known that the way entities update their states over time has a major impact on their dynamics. In particular, depending on the chosen update schedule, the underlying dynamical systems may exhibit more or less asymptotic dynamical behaviours such as fixed points or limit cycles.

arxiv-2207-12090.title: Optimising MWA EoR data processing for improved 21 cm power spectrum measurements - fine-tuning ionospheric corrections DOI: 10.1017/pas.2026.xxx
arxiv-2207-12090.creator: J. Kariuki Chege 1,2, C. H. Jordan 1,2, C. Lynch 1,2, C. M. Trott 1,2 J. L. B. Line 1,2, B. Pindor 2,3, and S. Yoshiura 4,3,2
arxiv-2207-12090.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by J. Kariuki Chege 1,2, C. H. Jordan 1,2, C. Lynch 1,2, C. M. Trott 1,2 J. L. B. Line 1,2, B. Pindor 2,3, and S. Yoshiura 4,3,2. The redshifted cosmological 21 cm signal emitted by neutral hydrogen during the first billion years of the universe is much fainter relative to other galactic and extragalactic radio emissions, posing a great challenge towards detection of the signal.

arxiv-2208-14792.title: Applicability of Hydrodynamics in Hadronic Phase of Heavy-Ion Collisions
arxiv-2208-14792.creator: Ronald Scaria, Captain R. Singh, Raghunath Sahoo
arxiv-2208-14792.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ronald Scaria, Captain R. Singh, Raghunath Sahoo. The hadronic phase and its dynamics in relativistic heavy-ion collisions are topics of immense discussion. The hadronic phase contains various massive hadrons with an abundance of the lightest hadron, i.e., π \pi -mesons (pions). In this paper, we consider that pions are in the thermal equilibrium in the hadronic phase and use second-order viscous hydrodynamics for a medium of massive pions to obtain its expansion to the boundary of the kinetic freeze-out.

arxiv-2301-02320.title: Differential embeddings into algebras of topological stable rank 1 Thanks: IM CAS (RVO 67985840)
arxiv-2301-02320.creator: Tomasz Kania, Natalia Maślany
arxiv-2301-02320.description: Abstract . We identify a class of smooth Banach *-algebras that are differential subalgebras of commutative C*-algebras whose openness of multiplication is completely determined by the topological stable rank of the target C*-algebra. We then show that group algebras of Abelian groups of unbounded exponent fail to have uniformly open convolution.

arxiv-2402-19027.title: How to Train your Antivirus: RL-based Hardening through the Problem Space
arxiv-2402-19027.creator: Ilias Tsingenopoulos, Jacopo Cortellazzi, Branislav Bošanský, Simone Aonzo, Davy Preuveneers, Wouter Joosen, Fabio Pierazzi, Lorenzo Cavallaro
arxiv-2402-19027.description: Abstract . ML-based malware detection on dynamic analysis reports is vulnerable to both evasion and spurious correlations. In this work, we investigate a specific ML architecture employed in the pipeline of a widely-known commercial antivirus, with the goal to harden it against adversarial malware.

arxiv-2411-05691.title: Asterisk*: Keep it Simple
arxiv-2411-05691.creator: Andrew Semenov
arxiv-2411-05691.description: Abstract This paper describes Asterisk*, a compact GPT-based model for generating text embeddings. The model implements a minimalist architecture with two layers, two attention heads, and 256 embedding dimensions. Through knowledge distillation from larger pretrained models, we examine the trade-offs between model size and performance while reducing computational and memory requirements.

arxiv-2507-18349.title: Observation of Kibble-Zurek Behavior across Topological Transitions of a Chern Band in Ultracold Atoms
arxiv-2507-18349.creator: Huan Yuan, Chang-Rui Yi, Jia-Yu Guo, Xiang-Can Cheng, Rui-Heng Jiao, Jinyi Zhang, Shuai Chen, Jian-Wei Pan
arxiv-2507-18349.description: Abstract The Kibble-Zurek (KZ) mechanism renders a theoretical framework for elucidating the formation of topological defects across continuous phase transitions. Nevertheless, it is not immediately clear whether the KZ mechanism applies to topological phase transitions. The direct experimental study for such a topic is hindered by quenching a certain parameter over orders of magnitude in topological materials.

pmc-10736184.title: MAINTAINING PERSONHOOD AND AUTONOMY: A GROUNDED THEORY OF COMMUNITY-BASED HOSPICE CARE TRANSITIONS
pmc-10736184.creator: Catherine Mann, Suzanne Sullivan, Yu-Ping Chang
pmc-10736184.description: Supporting care transitions as decline occurs for patients facing serious illness and their families necessitates ongoing identification of person-centered, family-oriented goals. However, little is known about the process patients and caregivers undergo when making decisions while transitioning to home hospice care.

pmc-11351937.title: The Efficacy of Body-Weight Supported Treadmill Training and Neurotrophin-Releasing Scaffold in Minimizing Bone Loss Following Spinal Cord Injury
pmc-11351937.creator: Michael Weiser, Lindsay Stoy, Valerie Lallo, Sriram Balasubramanian, Anita Singh
pmc-11351937.description: Spinal cord injury (SCI) can lead to significant bone loss below the level of the lesion increasing the risk of fracture and increased morbidity. Body-weight-supported treadmill training (BWSTT) and transplantation strategies using neurotrophins have been shown to improve motor function after SCI.

pmc-11453178.title: 7058 Debunking the Bimodal Theory of Autoimmunity: Graves' Disease (GD) Hyperthyroidism and Hashimoto’s Disease (HD) Hypothyroidism Can Coexist on a Spectrum, a Case Series
pmc-11453178.creator: Aviva Atri-Schuller, Aleona C Zuzek, Abid Yaqub
pmc-11453178.description: Disclosure: A. Atri-Schuller: None. A.C. Zuzek: None. A. Yaqub: None.It is not uncommon for hyperthyroid patients to eventually become hypothyroid after prolonged periods of inflammation and hyperactivity, occasionally referred to as “burnt-out Graves.” However, going from a hypothyroid to a hyperthyroid state has been described as a rare phenomenon in the literature.

pmc-11794066.title: Uric acid to albumin ratio is a novel predictive marker for all-cause and cardiovascular death in diabetic patients: a prospective cohort study
pmc-11794066.creator: Shengnan Chen, Ming Zhang, Shouye Hu, Xiaolong Shao, Lin Liu, Zhi Yang, Kai Nan
pmc-11794066.description: BackgroundDiabetes is one of the leading causes of death with an increasing prevalence worldwide. Diabetes-related premature mortality is largely preventable and reversible if identified and managed early. Accordingly, we intend to investigate the predictive value of uric acid to albumin ratio (UAR) for all-cause and cardiovascular death in diabetic patients.

pmc-12403521.title: Underwater audiogram of the grey seal (Halichoerus grypus)
pmc-12403521.creator: Andreas Ruser, Kirstin Anderson Hansen, Magnus Wahlberg, Tobias Schaffeld, Ursula Siebert
pmc-12403521.description: The hearing sensitivity of two grey seals (Halichoerus grypus) was measured using a psychophysical staircase method from 0.125 to 64 kHz. Both animals had best hearing sensitivity at 4 kHz (43-44 dB re 1 µPa). Below 4 kHz, hearing thresholds differed. These first underwater audiograms using psychophysical methods demonstrate that high-frequency hearing in grey seals is comparable to other phocids.

pmc-12510434.title: Public Attitudes and Predictors of Public Awareness of Personal Digital Health Data Sharing for Research: Cross-Sectional Study in Japan
pmc-12510434.creator: Yasue Fukuda, Koji Fukuda, Andre Kushniruk
pmc-12510434.description: BackgroundAs digital technology advances, health-related data can be scientifically analyzed to predict illnesses. The analysis of international data collected during health examinations and health status monitoring, along with data collected during medical care delivery, can contribute to precision medicine and the public good. Understanding citizens’ attitudes and predictors of digital health data sharing is critical in promoting data-driven research.

pmc-12535170.title: Prevalence, radio-clinical patterns and factors associated with pulmonary tuberculosis among children with severe acute malnutrition: a cross-sectional study in Uganda
pmc-12535170.creator: Oliver Asiimwe, Grace Ndezi, Joshua Muhumuza, Faith Namukasa, Charles Mwendwa Mutisya, Salad Hassan Abdirahman, Ali Muhuyadin haji Abdifatah, Omar Mohamed Abdirizak, Said Ibrahim Amatarahman, Martin Nduwimana
pmc-12535170.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAlthough treatable, pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) has a significant morbidity and mortality. Children with malnutrition are immune compromised, which increases the morbidity and mortality of PTB. Literature from other countries has shown that the occurrence of malnutrition is significantly associated with tuberculosis, but there is a paucity of data about this subject in Uganda, yet throughout the past 15 years, Uganda’s rate of malnutrition reduction has been quite very slow.MethodsThis was a cross–sectional study among children aged 6–59 months with SAM at JRRH.

pmc-12553299.title: Factors associated with intention to use generative artificial intelligence in nursing practice: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12553299.creator: Jeongin Choe, Kyungmi Woo
pmc-12553299.description: BackgroundGenerative artificial intelligence (GAI) can be used to support healthcare professionals. An in-depth understanding of how healthcare professionals adopt and use GAI in practice is lacking. We aimed to identify the intention to use GAI in nursing practice, its application areas, and the key factors associated with this intention.

pmc-13008723.title: Prognostic value of the pretreatment pan-immune-inflammation value in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13008723.creator: Te Li, Genping Li
pmc-13008723.description: BackgroundThe prognostic significance of the pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma has been comprehensively documented. Nevertheless, its exact role remains ambiguous. The objective of this study is to perform a systematic exploration of the correlation between the pretreatment PIV and survival outcomes in this population.

pmc-13478610.title: MRI assessment of muscle damage after posterolateral versus SuperPATH approach for total hip arthroplasty
pmc-13478610.creator: Fengping Gan, Qibiao Zhang, Haoji Luo, Linjie Li, Xinxin Lin, Hao Qin
pmc-13478610.description: The minimally invasive SuperPATH approach for total hip arthroplasty (THA) is theorized to reduce soft tissue damage, but objective evidence comparing muscle injury to the conventional posterolateral approach (PLA) is lacking. uslaw-usc-t46-s12119.title: 46 U.S.C. § 12119 — Owners engaged primarily in leasing or financing transactions
uslaw-usc-t46-s12119.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t46-s12119.description: United States Code, Title 46 (Shipping); Part H (Identification Of Vessels); Chapter 121 (Documentation Of Vessels); Subchapter II (Endorsements And Special Documentation). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Definitions.— In this section: (1) Affiliate.— The term “affiliate” means, with respect to any person, any other person that is— (i) directly or indirectly controlled by, under common control with, or controlling that person.
